Commentary.Commentary: Right then! That's all from this game! Sri Lanka have taken the series 2-1 and go into the T20I series with a lot of confidence. South Africa, on the other hand, would be disappointed with this performance but they have some of the regular players back for the T20I series. The T20I series is set to begin on Friday, September 10th, 2021 at 8 pm local (2.30 pm GMT). Do join us then. Cheers and take care.

Dasun Shanaka, the Sri Lankan skipper, says that it is really pleasing as they have won a series after a long time. Adds that they have played really good cricket this series. Goes onto say that toss played a major role and winning it made a really good impact on this match. Tells that he thought that 230 would have been an ideal score but 203 turned out to be a very good score. Says that Maheesh Theekshana proved to be a decisive bowler and he is a bright prospect for them going forward. States that he should have stayed there with the bat more. Says that he wanted to bat more lower and he really wanted to contribute.

Keshav Maharaj, the South African skipper, says that the bowlers did really well and the wicket was slow. Tells that the batting did not go to plan. Credits Sri Lanka for playing really well. States that the first Powerplay set them back. Goes onto say that if you look at the first two games, the batters were very positive but it did not work in this game. On the mindset for the T20Is, Maharaj admits that it is back to the drawing board but also asserts that they will get a few senior players back in the T20I series.

Charith Asalanka, the Man of the Series, says that he is glad to be the Man of the Series and he is very happy. Adds that he made a plan to take singles and he enjoyed it. Adds that he feels that he did the job for his team. States that they were looking for 230 to 240 but when Hasaranga and Shanaka got out, they looked at getting to 220.

Dushmantha Chameera, the Man of the Match, says that the wicket was a bit slow and he tried to bowl good lengths consistently. Adds that he had rough injuries past few years and he tried to get himself fit and he practiced well the last few months.
Stay tuned for the presentation ceremony!

South Africa never looked like chasing this total down! They kept on losing wickets at regular intervals. Markram fell quickly while Hendricks and van der Dussen did not last long. Malan looked good till he was out there but he fell before rain stopped things for a while. There was no return from there as whoever came out to bat simply fell prey to the Sri Lankan bowlers. Overall, it was a pretty disappointing performance from the South African batsmen.

Sri Lanka rolled over South Africa pretty easily! They started brilliantly with the ball as Praveen Jayawickrama sent back Aiden Markram pretty early and then on a pitch which was not aiding the seamers, Dushmantha Chameera bowled beautifully and chipped in with two wickets. Then it was the debutant's show. Maheesh Theekshana simply bamboozled the batsmen with his mystery spin, taking 4 wickets. Hasaranga was brilliant as well while Charith Asalanka bowled well in his first over.

What a bowling performance and Sri Lanka have taken the series 2-1! The hosts have been absolutely brilliant and they also get some valuable points in the World Cup Super League. A simply sensational performance here and they deserve the series win. South Africa, on the other hand, crumbled and they will be disappointed with this performance.

Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Chandimal b Maheesh Theekshana

NOT OUT! Wickets missing! Nervous moment for Andile but what a review. That looked dead, if it was not bat. Flatter ball on middle, Phehlukwayo looked to defend with the bat behind his pad and was hit. Now, to the naked eye, it seemed like it hit the bat. But Sri Lanka put up an appeal for LBW and the finger went up. Phehlukwayo took the review after thinking for a while. The first thing the third umpire checks is whether there was an inside edge. The first replay shows that the ball hit the pad, then the bat and later, rolled to the on side. From that angle, it did seem like the angle will take the ball down the leg side, as Theekshana was bowling it from around the wicket. Then came the Ball Tracker which showed that it will miss the stumps, going down the leg side! Linde has to be credited for saving his partner here as he insisted on taking the review.

Update 7.50 pm (2.20 pm GMT) - Yipppeee! Great news. We are hearing from the middle is that the covers are completely off and the play should begin at 8 pm local (2.30 pm GMT)!

Update 7.20 pm (1.50 pm GMT) - Hmmm... this was coming. HD Ackermann mentioned on air that just before the start of the 9th over, he was seeing groundstaff near the covers, making some movement. He did not reckon that it will rain but if the Lankan groundstaff get a bit impatient, rain is around the corner. And it did arrive. It began as a light drizzle, which is why the umpires did not take the players off immediately. But just as Wiaan Mulder looked to take guard, the drizzle got heavier and covers were called upon. It has gotten heavier now and this might be a lengthy delay. Fingers crossed.
Wiaan Mulder walks in at number 6, replacing Janneman Malan. It is drizzling slightly, but the umpires have chosen to go on with the game.

OUT! CAUGHT! It is a catch and Malan goes! Theekshana strikes off his first delivery in international cricket. What a moment for him and he will be very happy. Tossed up outside off, Malan looks to drive but it goes off the outside edge to first slip where Dhananjaya de Silva takes the catch. Let's stop here for a moment and describe this in two different parts. First part. Is it a catch? Sri Lanka are celebrating. But Malan is going nowhere. He stands there, thinking that the ball has hit the ground and then gone to the fielder. The two umpires converge and then raise it upstairs, with the soft signal as OUT. Here comes the replay. Pretty straightforward. The bat has hit the ground and the ball has gone off the outside edge. Pretty sure, Malan would have felt the bat hitting the ground as a bump ball, hence, wanted confirmation. Now, the second part. How good a catch was that from Mr. Dhananjaya de Silva? Very, very, very. Magnificently brilliant. We are running short of adjectives. Yes, it was a spinner. Yes, the ball does come slowly as compared to that of a fast bowler. But this one, just flew right at his face. De Silva just showed his reflex action and at the right moment, got his hands in front of his face and the ball went right into those buckets. My word, that is simply sensational. Congratulations, Theekshana, but please honour Dhananjaya for that ripper of a catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Dhananjaya de Silva b Maheesh Theekshana
